propositions: The mutation-gate harness executes mutated code unsandboxed, allowing destructive mutations (e.g., removing guards from shell scripts) to cause real filesystem damage like rm -rf on protected directories.

Both test-executing subprocesses in execute_shard() (baseline pytest and mutmut run mutant test) must be wrapped in OS-enforced sandboxes with explicit allow-lists that exclude the venv to prevent mutants from dropping executable code into site-packages.

Sandbox enforcement must be functionally verified by observing denial (file absent, non-zero exit) rather than by inspecting constructed argv, and verified separately on each platform (macOS Seatbelt and Linux bwrap) and in CI versus workstation environments.

The HOME environment variable must be set to a non-existent path for sandboxed subprocesses to fail loudly if a mutant attempts home-directory writes, verified by running children and asserting the HOME they observe.

On workstations without a working sandbox mechanism the gate aborts non-zero naming REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED; on CI runners it proceeds unsandboxed with a warning, keyed on the CI environment variable.
The sandbox wrapper must preserve the existing --max-children 1 concurrency contract and the enforcement must work from a laptop with no CI involvement, using OS facilities invoked in-process.
